title: (No AI) John Deere launched an AI chatbot for farmers
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![A screenshot of John Deere’s JD AI chatbot interface](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/john-deere-jd-ai-featured.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

John Deere is testing a new ["JD" AI assistant](https://www.deere.com/en-us/privacy-data/data-services/your-data#meet-jd) that it says can help farmers make more money, with answers about best practices and historical trends that are based on their own data. It uses their "field, machine and operational data" to answer questions on topics like equipment settings, fuel usage, or harvest timing.

The press release didn't mention which AI technology is behind this platform. title: (No AI) Google Pics is like Canva, but with even more AI
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
![A screenshot of Google Pics generating a poster design for a street fair.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Google-Pics-rollout-hero.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Google wants Workspace users to edit and generate their business imagery with Pics. | Image: Google

Google has a new suite of creative design tools for Workspace users called Google Pics, which aims to make editing and generating "professional-grade" AI images less cumbersome for businesses. Built around Gemini and the Nano Banana generative AI model, Google Pics is designed to give more granular control over prompt-based image making and manipulation, allowing users to tap on specific objects or text, and describe what they want to change - features that may avoid the [ugly results](https://www.404media.co/we-are-living-in-a-chatgpt-flyer-pandemic/) that [chatbots are known to spit out](https://www.404media.co/these-are-the-worst-chatgpt-flyers-youve-sent-us/) for marketing imagery.

title: (No AI) You Know Who Really Hates AI? Insurance Claims Adjusters
